title: `openWorldHint`
description: Marks a tool as touching the open world: external, non deterministic effects.
question: Is the openWorldHint annotation present at each capture boundary?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
known_issues: Mastra and Pydantic AI retain the annotation outside their declared tool-definition capture objects; OpenAI Agents SDK does not.
Two framework adapters could not be measured against 2026-07-28, so missing evidence is not a support result.
why: A policy that reads the tool definition at the capture boundary can only tell that a call escapes the local system if the hint survives to that point. Where it is dropped, an external side effect looks the same as a local lookup.

notes.openai-agents: OpenAI Agents SDK: FunctionTool retains the MCP title only; the behavioral hint is not carried.
notes.pydantic-ai: Pydantic AI: retained in ToolDefinition.metadata['annotations']; not part of parameters_json_schema.
notes.mastra: Mastra 2.2.0: retained on the tool action's `mcp.annotations`; not part of the id, description or inputSchema the agent is handed.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): toolsFromDefinitions copies the server's openWorldHint onto the tool's app-side `metadata.annotations`, not into the description or inputSchema a provider adapter serializes. An app can read it; the model is not shown it.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: `mcpToFunctionTool` builds the `FunctionTool` from the MCP tool's name, description and inputSchema only. The `openWorldHint` annotation is not on the tool the model is handed and is not kept anywhere beside it.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools.build_tools` registers each tool as `Function(name, description, parameters=inputSchema)`; the tool's annotations, title, icons and `outputSchema` are not carried, so `openWorldHint` reaches neither the model nor the agent.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: `Tool.from_mcp_tool` builds a `dspy.Tool` from the MCP tool's name, description and `inputSchema` properties only; the tool's annotations, title, icons and `outputSchema` are on no `Tool` field and in no dict the LM is handed, so `openWorldHint` is lost.
notes.langchain_js: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): `MCPAdapter.listTools` keeps the server's annotations on the tool's app-side `metadata.annotations`, but the function tool `convertToOpenAITool` builds for the provider carries name, description and parameters only, so the model never sees `openWorldHint`.
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): the provider tool carries name, description and parameters only, and the runtime's permission request names title and `readOnly`. `openWorldHint` is not kept anywhere.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: MCP tool annotations reach `ToolSpecification.metadata()` only; the `ToolSpecification` AiServices hands the `ChatModel` carries name, description and parameters, so the model never sees `openWorldHint`.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `convertTool` builds the `FunctionDeclaration` from the tool's name, description, `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` only, and `mcpTool` keeps no other field of the `*mcp.Tool`, so `annotations.openWorldHint` is gone after listing.
notes.ms_agent_framework_dotnet: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): `McpClientTool` passes the model only the MCP tool's name, description, `inputSchema` (as `JsonSchema`) and `outputSchema` (as `ReturnJsonSchema`). It keeps the MCP `Tool` it was built from as the public `ProtocolTool` property, so `openWorldHint` is retained in framework metadata but never reaches the model.
